text:
Sam (Acme): Hey team, we're seeing a sudden spike of 429s for our project despite not hitting the per-project quota. Happening since ~10:12am UTC. Example response:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "detail": "ip_quota_exceeded",
  "request_id": "req_6a2f..."
}

We're using a proxy that pins a small pool of egress IPs shared across multiple projects. Project id: proj-1234, API key: sk-live-abc123. Can you help? We weren't getting 429s before the traffic spike.

Mike (Support): Thanks Sam. Can you paste a few request_ids and the exact time window? Also are you rotating API keys per request or reusing the same key behind the proxy?

Sam (Acme): Request IDs: req_6a2f2, req_6a2f3, req_6a2f9. Times around 2065432090-2065432140. We reuse the same API key per project; the proxy multiplexes many customer sessions over the same API key and 3 egress IPs.

Mike (Support): Reproducing now with your project id + key in a sandbox. Quick test curl I ran:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

I'm hitting 429s after ~120 requests/min. Response includes "ip_quota" in the detail tag.

Ana (SRE): Pinging about quota precedence. We have two limit dimensions in the rate-limiter: per-key (api_key_quota) and per-egress-ip (ip_quota). The intended evaluation order is:
1) org-level quota
2) ip-based quota
3) api-key/project quota

But I'm seeing evidence the current hotpath evaluates api-key first, then ip, which means shared IPs can get blocked even when project quota is available and org quota allows it. That mismatched precedence causes surprising 429s for customers behind proxies.

Lee (Product): Do we have any recent changes to the rate-limiter or rollout that could have flipped ordering?

Ana (SRE): We rolled a perf patch last week to short-circuit per-key checks earlier to reduce memcache lookups. Patch ID: perf/rlv2-shortcircuit. It inadvertently moved api-key checks ahead of ip checks in the evaluation pipeline.

Mike (Support): Is there a quick workaround for Sam while we fix this? They can't move off the proxy quickly.

Ana (SRE): Short-term workarounds:
- Add the proxy egress IPs to the project's ip_allowlist (if tolerable from security) which bypasses ip_quota.
- Increase per-key quota temporarily to compensate (but this is risky if truly shared heavily).
- Configure the proxy to rotate across more IPs so per-ip load drops below threshold.

I'll attach a quick policy snippet to add to the allowlist:

```
# admin CLI
redwoodctl projects update proj-1234 --ip-allowlist 35.198.12.45,35.198.12.46
```

Sam (Acme): Allowlist is doable for now. We'll try that. Any ETA on the real fix?

Ana (SRE): Escalating to a hotfix. Root cause: evaluation ordering bug introduced by perf patch. Plan:
- Revert the short-circuit change in the next patch (hotfix branch) -> test in staging (1 hour)
- Canary roll to 10% -> observe ip_quota metrics (2 hours)
- Full rollout if green (4 hours)

I've created an incident ticket: INC-2451 (internal) linking to the PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rl/PR-5412

ratebot: Alert: project proj-1234 exceeded 80% of ip_quota on 3 egress IPs (35.198.12.45, 35.198.12.46, 35.198.12.47) — triggered at 2065432120

Mike (Support): I've shared the allowlist CLI with Sam and turned on a temporary per-key bump for proj-1234 until the hotfix lands.

Sam (Acme): Allowlist added, testing now. After 5 minutes traffic looks normal, no 429s. Thanks.

Lee (Product): We should follow up with a postmortem and a change to the rate-limiter tests to enforce evaluation ordering. Also consider an admin-visible note in Console explaining ip vs key scoping to reduce confusion.

Ana (SRE): Agreed. Will add test coverage and a Console tooltip. Assigning follow-ups: RL-678 (tests), RL-679 (console copy). I'll update INC-2451 with runbook and timeline.

Mike (Support): Sam — we'll keep the per-key bump until the hotfix is fully rolled. Will post an update here when INC-2451 progresses.

Sam (Acme): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please include whether any billing was impacted (we saw a slight token spike). We'll need that for our billing reconciliation.

Ana (SRE): We'll capture the token counts and any overage. If there's billing impact we'll route to billing ops for adjustment. Adding note to INC-2451.

Mike (Support): Closing loop for now — marking this thread as monitored. Reopen if you see 429s after hotfix rollout. :thumbsup:

Sam (Acme): Confirmed no 429s after the allowlist. Thanks everyone — please ping when the postmortem is ready.
